summary: Commissioned cold refuter pass over post-integrity method v2 (compiler redesign cf9e2ab, per the 12:01 disposition)

verdicts.question: (1a) v1 FATAL 1 — the population source named no instrument that exists. Does v2's shipped instrument actually answer it, and is v2's description of that instrument true at the bytes?
verdicts.finding: An instrument now exists, and v2 makes a FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT IT in the section that answers the fatal. (a) THE CENTRAL SENTENCE IS REFUTED BY THE FILE IT DESCRIBES. post-integrity-method-v2-0813.md:60-61 reads '✅ The record is written by THE ACT THAT SENDS (same command, same `{ }`, no second decision), so the population is a fact rather than a reconstruction.' At the bytes there is no shared `{ }`: bus_send.sh:55 is `{ printf '\n'; cat "$SUBST"; } >> "$BUS"` and bus_send.sh:58-60 is a SEPARATE `printf ... >> "$LOG"`. Two acts wearing one script. The verdict file's repair specified the fix verbatim — 'inside the same `{ }` as the redirection' — and it was not done; the doc claims it anyway. bus_send.sh:2 and :57 assert the same falsehood about themselves. (b) THE SCRIPT'S OWN LINE 60 IS THE PROOF THERE IS A SECOND DECISION: `|| { echo "WARNING: APPEND LANDED BUT SEND RECORD FAILED -- population now incomplete"; exit 5; }`. MEASURED (T1, scratch bus): log path in a nonexistent directory → post lands on the bus, no send-log line, EXIT=5. A SIGKILL, terminal close, or full disk between :55 and :58 produces the same state with no warning at all. (c) THE FAILURE IS IN THE INVISIBLE DIRECTION, WHICH IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN v1. The population is now a SUBSET of the real sends. §5's conservation identity (:130-132) runs over the send log, so a send that never got logged is not LISTED, not PROCESSED, and not in any bucket — it is invisible to every clause in the file. §2:71-72 covers a LOST log ('say so and stop') and says nothing about a SHORT log, which is the failure the script actually implements. (d) THE POPULATION IS CURRENTLY EMPTY AND UNDISCLOSED. `find ~/projects/claude -iname '*sendlog*'` → nothing. `grep -c 'SENT   stamp=' FLEET.md` → 0. bus_send.sh has never been run against the real bus. So 'POPULATION := the SEND LOG' (:56) denotes the empty set today, and all 4,353 posts already on FLEET.md (12,088,239 bytes) are outside it permanently. §7 discloses a relight limit but never this one. (e) THE LOG PATH IS AN UNPINNED ARGUMENT. §1:49 names the WRITER, not the FILE; the spec never gives a canonical path. MEASURED (T2): three sends, third with a one-character typo in $3 → `>>` silently creates a second log; SENDLOG.tsv 2 lines, SNEDLOG.tsv 1 line, 5 posts on the bus, exit 0, no warning. 'The send log' is the same shape of undefined noun as v1's 'the send path'. (f) NOTHING DISTINGUISHES $BUS FROM $LOG. bus_send.sh:40 checks only `[ -f "$BUS" ]`. Transposing args 2 and 3 appends the post body to the send log and writes a TSV record into FLEET.md, with a green exit.
verdicts.repair: (1) Strike :60-61 and replace with what the code does: 'the record is written by a SECOND command in the same script; a crash or a log-write failure between them leaves a post on the bus with no record, and the population is then a subset.' (2) INVERT THE ORDER so the failure direction is visible: write an INTENT line to the log BEFORE the append and a completion mark after, so a crash yields a claimed send with no post — detectable as LOST — instead of a post with no claim, which nothing can detect. (3) Pin one canonical log path inside the script; refuse a $LOG that does not already exist rather than creating it. (4) Refuse if $BUS and $LOG are transposed (require the log to be the TSV, the bus the .md).

verdicts.question: (1b) v1 FATAL 2 — the four outcomes were neither exhaustive nor exclusive. Are v2's outcomes a true partition, is the epistemic axis genuinely separated, and is NOT-FOUND actually restored?
verdicts.finding: The core fatal IS answered — this is real repair, not renaming: SEND and DRAFT populations are separated (:82-87), NOT-FOUND is restored as its own status distinct from never-posted with the false-clean mechanism stated (:92-93), the epistemic axis is pulled out as a separate field (:84), UNCLASSIFIED is added and required to be zero or enumerated (:94-98), and a duplicate check is mandated (:99). Three residues, one of which is the exact v1 defect reappearing inside the repair. (a) `LOST` IS A NEW UNDEFINED LOAD-BEARING NOUN. :83 lists five statuses; :92-98 gloss only NOT-FOUND and UNCLASSIFIED; `LOST` appears once in the whole file and is never defined, and §1 — titled 'THE NOUNS, DEFINED OR MARKED OPEN' (:43) — does not cover it. With the anchor now a recorded byte offset, LOST and NOT-FOUND have no stated boundary. v1's Q6(c) fatal was 'undefined load-bearing terms'; v2 introduces a fresh one in the section answering it. (b) §3 AND §5 CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. §5:130-132 mandates `LISTED = PROCESSED = Σ(status buckets)`, refusing on inequality. §3:84 makes `examined: yes/no` a SEPARATE AXIS, not a status. An unexamined send therefore has no status bucket, so Σ(buckets) < PROCESSED and the identity REFUSES on any run that leaves anything unexamined — i.e. the epistemic axis can never be exercised. The only escape is to give unexamined sends a status, which re-mixes the two axes and is precisely the defect :89-90 says v2 fixed. The two flagship repairs are mutually inconsistent as written. (c) THE MANDATORY DUPLICATE CHECK IS BROKEN BY v2's OWN INSTRUMENT. :99 requires 'exactly ONE region matches per send-log line'. MEASURED (T3, five concurrent bus_send.sh against one scratch bus — the fleet's own declared regime per :96): recorded offsets were 31, 32, 32, 4072, 4072 while the true header offsets were 32, 4072, 8110, 12150, 16188. Two pairs of send-log lines carry IDENTICAL offsets, so two lines resolve to the same region and the mandatory check fires on posts that landed perfectly intact; three true headers were never recorded at all.
verdicts.repair: Define LOST against NOT-FOUND explicitly (suggest: NOT-FOUND = the recorded offset does not resolve to a header; LOST = it resolves and the region is absent/empty) or mark it OPEN in the §1 table. Reconcile §3 with §5: state the identity as LISTED = PROCESSED = Σ(status buckets) + UNEXAMINED, so the epistemic axis is countable without being a status. Make the duplicate check conditional on a locked append (see Q2), or state that it cannot run under contention.

verdicts.question: (1c) v1 FATAL 3 — the warrant was false. Is §0's correction honest, complete, and accurately sourced?
verdicts.finding: Substantially yes, and this is the strongest section in the file — but it commits a small version of the sin it corrects, and it names a defect that then vanishes. VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY RECORD: FLEET.md:85153 is silicon's 08:28:51 self-correction of their own 08:27 post; FLEET.md:85172 is compiler's 08:38:37 first offer of the method — ten minutes later, as :22 says; FLEET.md:85345 is the maestro's 08:50:27 closing order, confirming :38-39's correction that THREE seats ran instruments (silicon 85244, compiler 85212, math 85268/85291) and the fourth header ran none. :24-26 ('THIS METHOD HAS NEVER FIRED ON A LIVE CORRUPTION') is accurate. (a) OVER-PRECISION INSIDE THE ACCURACY SECTION. :20-21 writes '08:27:xx' — conceding the seconds are unknown — and then asserts '66 seconds later'. 66 is derivable only from an 08:27:45 that the file itself marks as unknown; the primary source (FLEET.md:85153) says 'WITHIN NINETY SECONDS'. A stated interval the cited record does not support, in the section whose entire job is not doing that. (b) §0 NAMES A DEFECT THAT NOTHING ELSE IN THE FILE CARRIES. :32-34 makes half the indictment 'an unknown BASE RATE and unexamined AIM — no measurement of how often the thing this detects actually occurs.' No later section measures, mandates measuring, or even mentions base rate, and §7 — the list of what v2 does not claim — omits it entirely. The cf9e2ab correction is confined to §0, so a reader who quotes §7 as the humility list quotes it without the sharper half of the indictment. That is v1:111 ('State it inside the verdict or the verdict will be quoted without it') applied to v2's own structure.
verdicts.repair: Change '66 seconds later' to 'inside ninety seconds, per the correcting post's own words (FLEET.md:85153)' — the seconds of the 08:27 post are not in the record. Add a §7 bullet: 'THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED. One real corruption in the whole record, self-found. Nothing here measures how often the detected event occurs, so no cost/benefit argument for mandating this method is available.'

verdicts.question: (2) bus_send.sh at the bytes: is the send record written by the same act as the append, what happens on partial failure, and does it introduce a new corruption vector? Tested against a scratch bus with an adversarial 21,305-byte / 314-line body carrying %, backticks, $(...), apostrophes, fences, unicode, sed metachars and a literal @@STAMP@@.
verdicts.finding:
NO on the same act (see Q1a). The instrument additionally SILENTLY CORRUPTS BODIES AND CERTIFIES THE CORRUPTION, and its recorded anchor is wrong by one byte and stale under contention. (a) THE MUTATING STAGE IS STILL INVISIBLE TO THE RECEIPT — v1's first unassigned kill, unanswered and undisclosed. bus_send.sh:44 runs `sed "s|@@STAMP@@|$STAMP|g"` GLOBALLY over the whole body; :51 hashes the SUBSTITUTED file. MEASURED: my body carried 3 literal @@STAMP@@; the bus carried 0. All three were rewritten, including two that were CONTENT — 'LITERAL PLACEHOLDER AS CONTENT ... @@STAMP@@ must survive' → '... 08/13 12:33:13 must survive', and the fenced line `sed "s|@@STAMP@@|$STAMP|g" file` → `sed "s|08/13 12:33:13|$STAMP|g" file`. Because BODY_SHA is taken after the substitution, any verifier reports INTACT. The guard at :47-49 is the OPPOSITE guard — it refuses when the placeholder SURVIVED, never when it was eaten. bus_send.sh CONTAINS 4 LITERAL @@STAMP@@ (lines 16, 18, 44, 47): THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEND ITSELF, OR ANY POST DOCUMENTING THIS METHOD, WITHOUT SILENT CORRUPTION THAT ITS OWN RECEIPT CALLS CLEAN. (b) THE RECORDED OFFSET POINTS AT THE WRONG BYTE, AND THE SPEC'S REGION RULE THEN RETURNS ONE BYTE. :53 records `wc -c < BUS` = 47; :55 writes `printf '
'` first, so the header lands at byte 48. Applying §4:108 literally — `region := bus[recorded_offset .. next ^\[ header | EOF]` — the scan finds the post's OWN header and the region is 1 byte. MEASURED on NC0, the cleanest possible send: literal region length 1, sha mismatch. NC0 CANNOT PASS AGAINST THE TWO COMMITTED ARTIFACTS. Only an undocumented correction (+1, then scan past the post's own header line) matches, and only when no body line begins with '['. (c) REGION TRUNCATION ON A QUOTED HEADER — and the half it drops is the evidence half. MEASURED (T4): a post quoting a peer's header at column 0 → region truncated to 97 bytes; the orphaned tail was `[08/13 08:42:11, silicon ...]
and here is the evidence that must not be lost`. Verdict CORRUPTED on an intact post, and the bytes excluded are exactly 'the CLAIM survives and its EVIDENCE does not', which is the failure class this method exists to prevent — now manufactured by the verifier. On the real bus: 4,745 column-0 '[' lines, of which 3,304 match a zero-padded stamped header and 1,441 do not; 392 are not blank-line separated. v2 gives no grammar for 'header', so the rule does not resolve on the corpus it targets. (d) CONCURRENCY: the recorded anchor is captured at :53 and used at :55, with no lock. MEASURED (T3): 3 of 5 recorded offsets did not point at their own header; offset=32 was captured MID-APPEND (after another seat's `printf '
'`, before its `cat` flushed), so a recorded offset can point into the middle of another seat's body. (e) A GREEN EXIT WITH NO HASH. No `set -o pipefail`; :51's pipeline is unchecked. MEASURED (T6, failing shasum first on PATH): SHA field EMPTY, EXIT=0, printed 'SENT'. That send is unverifiable forever and nothing flags it. (f) 'REFUSED' IS A LIE ABOUT STATE. :55's `|| exit 4` prints 'REFUSED: append failed' — but a `cat` that fails mid-write (ENOSPC) has already put bytes on the bus. The operator is told nothing happened. (g) MINOR, MEASURED: LINES undercounts on a source with no trailing newline (logged 2, true 3 — T7); the TSV has no escaping, so a tab in the source path yields a 7-field record where the schema has 6 (T8); STAMP (:42) carries no year or timezone.
verdicts.repair: (1) Assert the mutation: `diff "$SRC" "$SUBST"` must show ONLY stamp-token changes, and refuse if the source contains an @@STAMP@@ off the header line — or use a placeholder that cannot occur in prose. (2) Record the offset AFTER the append as `wc -c` minus the substituted length, or drop the leading `printf '\n'` and record the true header offset; either way spec and script must agree to the byte. (3) Define 'header' as a regex in §4 and record the region END offset too, so the region is bounded by two recorded facts and no scan is needed. (4) flock the bus across offset-capture + append + record. (5) `set -o pipefail`; refuse on an empty BODY_SHA. (6) Change exit 4's text to 'APPEND MAY HAVE PARTIALLY LANDED'.

verdicts.question: (3) Are NC0–NC8 controls of the right form under rider 4 clause (i) — do they traverse the real pipeline — and is NC8 actually send-side?
verdicts.finding: The ✅ column cannot be reproduced from anything committed, and one of its entries is refuted by the committed artifacts. (a) NO VERIFIER EXISTS. `git show --stat 933184f` and `cf9e2ab` add exactly two files: bus_send.sh and the .md. bus_send.sh:34 states outright 'it does not verify anything.' NC0–NC7 all assert VERIFIER outputs — INTACT, CORRUPTED, NOT-FOUND, 'must not match', 'must REFUSE', 'must print SKIPPED and conservation must REFUSE' — from an instrument that is not in the repository, with no receipt, no inputs, and no hashes committed. This is v1's third unassigned kill verbatim, unanswered — and it lands in the SAME REPOSITORY 2.5 hours after 52e2549 ('a behavioural bridge only holds if the COMPARER is unchanged between runs, and mine was an unsaved inline script'), 24920e5 ('PIN THE COMPARER'), and 364c918 (anchor inputs with sha256 + sizes). A verdict from an unsaved comparer is not a verdict, by this fleet's own ruling, made that morning. (b) NC0's ✅ IS REFUTED BY THE COMMITTED PAIR. Run bus_send.sh, apply §4:108 as written: the region is 1 byte and NC0 fails (measured, Q2b). Therefore the comparer that produced ✅ was NOT the shipped region rule — which is exactly rider 4(i), 'a control that does not traverse the instrument's own pipeline is not a control' (FLEET.md:84926), violated inside the suite whose stated purpose is to enforce rider 4(i). Either NC0's green is against a different rule than the one shipped, or §4:108 is wrong; both are fatal to the column. (c) NC5's GREEN IS IMPORTED FROM THE v1 PIPELINE. :150 marks it '✅ (run 08:48)' in a column headed 'run 2026-08-13' — that is compiler's v1-era read-side check, a different instrument on a different population. Carrying an old green into a new suite is the same rider 4(i) failure. (d) NC6 IS HALF-CONTROLLED. :151 requires REFUSE on an empty source OR region and marks it '✅ guarded'. Only the source side is guarded (bus_send.sh:39); the region side has no guard because no verifier exists. The empty-vs-empty comparison that killed the author's first v1 receipt is still unguarded on the side where it actually occurred. (e) NC8 IS SEND-SIDE IN FORM AND UNDER-DECLARED IN SUBSTANCE. It does run the real tool — genuine progress, and the one control that never existed. But :163 declares ONE substitution, 'the destination path'. It silently substitutes three more, and all three carry the measured failures: the CONTENTION REGIME (one writer vs the five the file itself names at :96 — where 3/5 recorded offsets went wrong), the FILE SIZE (a fresh scratch file vs 12,088,239 bytes), and the HEADER GRAMMAR (a clean scratch bus vs 1,441 non-conforming column-0 '[' lines). (f) NC8's HAZARD LIST OMITS THE ONE HAZARD THE VERDICT NAMED IN WRITING. :161-162 lists 'fences, apostrophes, %, $(...), backticks and unicode' — no literal @@STAMP@@, which the verdict file's first unassigned kill named explicitly and which I demonstrated lands as silent corruption with a matching hash. NC8 is v1's own §5 thesis executed a second time: a control tests the axis you wrote it for.
verdicts.repair: Strike every ✅ in the §6 table until (1) a verifier is committed to docs/ledger-tools/ with its own sha recorded, (2) each control's inputs and outputs are committed as a receipt file, and (3) NC0 passes against the SHIPPED region rule and the SHIPPED instrument — today it does not. Re-declare NC8's substitutions as four, not one. Add NC9: a body containing a literal @@STAMP@@ as content must not be silently rewritten. Add NC10: two concurrent sends must not record the same offset.

verdicts.question: (4) Is each §7 humility claim stated accurately — neither over- nor under-claimed?
verdicts.finding: Two of four accurate, one over-claimed and refuted by measurement, one wrong in both directions and omitting the dominant limit. (a) :167 'It has never fired on a live corruption. Neither had v1.' — ACCURATE, sourced, correctly cross-referenced to §0. (b) :168-169 '`>>` IS NOT ATOMIC and v2 does not pretend otherwise — The send log makes interleaving DETECTABLE (offset + length + hash), not absent.' — OVER-CLAIMED AND REFUTED. Under the fleet's own declared regime (five writers, no lock), the recorded offset is captured before the act and goes stale: measured 3/5 offsets pointing at the wrong header, two duplicate offset pairs, and one offset captured mid-append pointing into another seat's body. What the log makes detectable is not interleaving — it is a HASH MISMATCH INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM REAL CORRUPTION, verbatim the v1 Q3(c) defect ('cannot distinguish my body lost a block from my extraction window is misaligned') that §4 claims to have cured. On this axis v2 is arguably worse than v1: v1 SEARCHED for its header and would find the right one; v2 TRUSTS a recorded number that contention makes wrong. (c) :170-171 'It does not survive a relight: the send log is per-machine and per-seat, and a fresh head inherits no population.' — WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The log is a file at a path passed as an argument; written under saltworks/ it survives a relight and is git-trackable, and because the sha is recorded the SOURCE need not survive at all — which was v1's actual relight problem, and v2 largely solved it without noticing. Meanwhile the real scope limit is absent from §7 entirely: NOTHING SENT BY ANY OTHER MEANS IS COVERED, EVER. bus_send.sh has zero real uses, no send log exists anywhere on the machine, and the 4,353 posts already on FLEET.md are permanently outside the population — with no gate, no enforcement, and nothing stopping any seat from continuing to `>>` the bus directly. (d) :172 'A green run is the absence of the failure modes NC0–NC8 name, and nothing else.' — ACCURATE AS A SENTENCE and the best line in §7, but it inherits §6's unreproducible ✅ column, so today it certifies the absence of failure modes that were never demonstrably tested. (e) OMITTED FROM §7 ALTOGETHER: no remediation clause exists anywhere in v2 (what does an auditor DO on CORRUPTED? the only lived remedy is a correction post, which adds a round — the activity the freeze existed to stop); the mutating sed stage is still invisible to the receipt; the base rate is unmeasured (named in §0:32-34, dropped here).
verdicts.repair: Rewrite bullet 2: 'the send log records an offset captured BEFORE the append, so under concurrent writers it can be stale or point into another post; interleaving then presents as CORRUPTED and is not distinguishable from real corruption. Until the append is locked, this is a known false-positive source.' Replace bullet 3 with: 'it covers ONLY posts sent through bus_send.sh. Today that is zero posts; the entire existing bus is outside the population and always will be. Nothing prevents a seat from appending directly.' Add bullets for remediation, the mutating stage, and the base rate.

verdicts.question: (5) What does v2 newly introduce that v1 did not have — new single points of failure, new corruption vectors, new undefined terms?
verdicts.finding: v2 introduces a mutating writer on the live bus and a population whose failure direction is undetectable, and presents both as facts. (a) A NEW CORRUPTION VECTOR AIMED AT THE FLEET'S OWN SUBJECT MATTER. v1 had no shipped writer; v2 ships one that rewrites every occurrence of @@STAMP@@ anywhere in the body (bus_send.sh:44) and hashes the result (:51). The class of post most likely to contain that token is a post ABOUT THIS METHOD — the exact traffic this fleet is generating. Demonstrated: 3 of 3 literal occurrences rewritten, receipt clean, and bus_send.sh's own 4 occurrences mean the instrument cannot transmit itself. (b) A NEW SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE, HALF-DISCLOSED. :71-72 honestly flags the log as single-copy and unreplicated, and states the right rule for a LOST log. It does not flag the SHORT log, which is the case the script actually implements (exit 5 at bus_send.sh:60) and the one nothing downstream can detect — a subset population presented at :61 as 'a fact rather than a reconstruction'. v1's population was known-bad and said so under the verdict; v2's is silently short and asserted sound. That is a regression in epistemic posture even as it is an advance in mechanism. (c) THE DRAFT POPULATION HAS NO INSTRUMENT AND CANNOT ACQUIRE ONE UNDER v2's OWN RULES. :86-87 creates a DRAFT population ('files never passed to a send'). The only way to enumerate files-that-were-never-sent is a directory listing, which v1:27/:37 forbade as the original sin and which v2 nowhere un-forbids. v2 solved the numerator's instrument problem and recreated v1's denominator problem in a new bucket. (d) NEW UNDEFINED TERM: `LOST` (:83), never glossed, absent from the §1 nouns table. (e) NEW INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the epistemic axis (:84) and the conservation identity (:130-132) cannot both hold (Q1b). (f) NEW UNPINNED NOUN: 'the SEND LOG' has no canonical path, `>>` creates one silently on a typo, and $BUS/$LOG are interchangeable without a guard. (g) DROPPED WITHOUT NOTICE: v1's §3:52-55 — 'A QUOTED HEREDOC IS NOT ENOUGH AND THAT IS THE COMMON MISREADING... it protects the body from EXPANSION and still hands it to the shell to PARSE' — is the single most transferable operational lesson in v1 and appears nowhere in v2. A reader adopting v2 without using bus_send.sh receives no send-side guidance at all, and v2 never says v1's §3 was superseded.
verdicts.repair: Add a §8 'WHAT v2 INTRODUCES THAT v1 DID NOT' listing the mutating writer, the short-log failure, and the unpinned log path. Carry v1:52-55 forward verbatim as the send-side rule for anyone not using the tool. Either give the DRAFT population an instrument or delete it and say drafts are unenumerable under this method. Define LOST.

unassignedKills: DO NOT RUN bus_send.sh AGAINST FLEET.md UNTIL THE SUBSTITUTION IS FIXED. Its first real use on a post about this method silently rewrites that post and certifies it INTACT. The instrument is one command away from manufacturing, on the live bus, the exact corruption class it was built to prevent — and it would be undetectable by every clause in the file it ships with.

NO REMEDIATION CLAUSE ANYWHERE IN v2, and v1's kill on this was never assigned either. Nothing states what an auditor DOES on CORRUPTED. There is no rollback, no retraction form, no rule against reposting. The only lived remedy is a correction post, which adds a round — the activity the 08:50 freeze existed to stop. A reader can finish v2 believing the method prevents something; it detects, after the bytes are public.

THE SPEC AND THE INSTRUMENT DO NOT COMPOSE UNDER ANY READING, AND NOBODY RAN THEM TOGETHER. §4:108's region rule applied to bus_send.sh's own output yields a 1-byte region on every send. The only reading that works requires two undocumented corrections (+1 byte, then scan past the post's own header) and still breaks on any body line starting with '['. This is not a subtle interaction — it fails on the simplest possible input, which means the anchor half of the redesign was never executed end-to-end even once. §6 nonetheless marks NC0 green.

THE INSTRUMENT HAS NO DRY-RUN AND NO ARGUMENT-SHAPE GUARD. bus_send.sh:40 checks only that $BUS exists. Transposing args 2 and 3 appends a post body into the send log and writes a TSV record into FLEET.md, exit 0. For a tool whose whole purpose is that the population is trustworthy, nothing distinguishes the population file from the destination file.

THE SEND-LOG STAMP CARRIES NO YEAR AND NO TIMEZONE (bus_send.sh:42, `+%m/%d %H:%M:%S`). The log is the population and its human-readable key is not unique or orderable across a year boundary. The offset is the real key, which is fine — but §2:57 lists the stamp first and §4:120-121 makes the stamp the thing verified against the log, so the weakest field is load-bearing in the one place v2 added a verification.

v2 IS NOT SELF-DESCRIBING ABOUT ITS OWN RECEIPTS. §6's table has a column headed 'run 2026-08-13' with nine ✅ and one parenthetical '(run 08:48)'. No receipt file, no comparer, no inputs, no hashes are committed — while the commit message asserts 'Controls run, not promised.' The document's own §0 indicts v1 for a warrant that claimed more than the record supports; §6 is the same shape of claim, one section apart, and it is the section a future reader will cite when adopting.

GOOD FAITH NOTED, AND IT MATTERS FOR THE DISPOSITION: this is a genuine cold redesign, not a rename. §0's warrant correction is accurate against the primary record and volunteered against its author's interest; NOT-FOUND is truly restored; the epistemic axis is truly split; the anchor is defined rather than hand-waved; controls are mandated rather than lamented; NC8 is a real send-side control that never existed; §2:71 and §7:167 disclose limits that would have been easy to omit; and NC7 was closed while writing rather than shipped as a gap, WITH a control on the control. Three of the six v1 questions are substantively answered. The fatals above are about the gap between what the file CLAIMS about its own artifacts and what those artifacts DO — which is, precisely and uncomfortably, the file's own subject.
